verification_report.summary:
The submitted v2 supplement is correct under the stated checked production inputs. The local lemma is valid: distributional differentiation of θ+dd^c u=aγ, followed by wedging with γ^(n-2), gives a first-order system da=B-aC. In complex dimension n>=2 the wedge map on real one-forms is invertible, so L1 bootstrap gives a smooth a; elliptic regularity then gives a smooth u. The restriction n>=2 is genuinely needed for this proof mechanism.

For the corollary, the attained-threshold theorem supplies a genuine subsolution without BMP, positive lower mass, or root-tail assumptions. A smooth strictly positive maximizing normalized current has the smooth Gauduchon root T=γ^(n-1). Trace saturation gives A∧γ^(n-1)=aγ^n. Positivity makes all coefficient measures of A absolutely continuous with L^n matrix density. The trace inequality is available for every smooth Hermitian test form. A countable dense family of locally constant positive matrices, extended to global metrics, makes the pointwise inequalities simultaneous; finite-dimensional determinant duality gives det(H)^(1/n)>=a. The trace equality gives the reverse AM-GM bound with the exact 1/n normalization. Equality forces H=aI, including on {a=0}, hence A=aγ as currents. This uses only a determinant of a measurable matrix after absolute continuity and never identifies it with a nonlinear current product.

The lemma therefore makes every threshold subsolution smooth, makes f^(1/n)=b^(-1/n)a(γ^n/dV)^(1/n) a.e. equal to a smooth nonnegative function, and only then gives the smooth exact equation. Repeating the argument for each threshold subsolution gives the same aγ and thus constant differences on connected compact X. The final smooth strictly positive-density observation uses the smooth dual formula only in that stated regime. No direct external-paper citation is introduced in v2; all named citations are exact internal production dependencies, whose scopes match the applications.
